_doc: Oil and gas fields, bitumen deposits and coal basins. Oil in barrels and gas in cubic metres of ultimately recoverable resource, coal in tonnes of production plus reserves (coal in-place resource is far larger). endowment is the total known resource, production to date plus remaining reserves (not only reserves, not oil or ore in place), to order of magnitude; where no defensible figure exists the key is omitted rather than guessed. conf: A = figure checked against a cited source in the audit, B = coordinate checked on Wikipedia and endowment approximate, C = from memory or a secondary summary. Entries with a status of modern are producing or recently producing; historic are worked out or pre-1800.

entries.name: Ghawar
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Ultimately recoverable oil, production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: IEA World Energy Outlook 2008: 66 Gb produced by 2007 + 74 Gb remaining = 140 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl (1/7.33 barrels per tonne of oil equivalent, Wikipedia Tonne of oil equivalent https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne_of_oil_equivalent) = 19.1 Gt; Aramco's 2010 statement was over 100 Gb originally
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Ghawar Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghawar_Field : "the oil production from Ghawar reached 66 Bbo in 2007, and that the remaining reserves are 74 Bbo" (IEA 2008)

entries.name: Greater Burgan
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Total potential recoverable oil estimated 66 to 75 Gb; midpoint 70.5 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl (1/7.33 barrels per toe, Wikipedia Tonne of oil equivalent) = 9.62 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Greater Burgan, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Burgan : "total potential production of recoverable oil has been estimated as between 66 and 75 billion barrels"

entries.name: Safaniya
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves around 37 Gb (the infobox labels the same number oil in place; undated) x 0.1364 t/bbl = 5.05 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Safaniya Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safaniya_Field : "Its reserves amount to around 37 billion barrels"

entries.name: Ahwaz-Asmari
entries.source: Coordinate: Ahvaz city per Wikipedia. Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Recoverable oil 37 Gb (infobox; 65.5 Gb in place) x 0.1364 t/bbl = 5.05 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Ahvaz Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahvaz_Field : "Recoverable oil 37,000 million barrels"

entries.name: Gachsaran
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia quotes 52.9 billion barrels, which is closer to oil in place; recoverable is a fraction of it, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Recoverable oil 23.7 Gb (infobox; 52.9 Gb in place) x 0.1364 t/bbl = 3.23 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Gachsaran oil field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gachsaran_oil_field : "Recoverable oil 23,700 million barrels"

entries.name: Prudhoe Bay
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia: about 25 billion barrels originally in place; recoverable about half, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Total recoverable 16 Gb (produced 12 Gb as of 28 March 2013 + remaining 4 Gb) x 0.1364 t/bbl = 2.18 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Prudhoe Bay Oil Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudhoe_Bay_Oil_Field : "Produced: 12 billion barrels ... as of March 28, 2013 Total recoverable: 16 billion barrels"

entries.name: Daqing
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Cumulative production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Produced over 10 Gb since 1960 x 0.1364 t/bbl = 1.36 Gt; reserves not given (infobox recoverable 3.6 Gb is below the production), so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Daqing Oil Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daqing_Oil_Field : "has produced over 10 billion barrels (1.6 x 10^9 m3) of oil since"

entries.name: Cantarell
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Pemex reported about 12.2 billion barrels produced to October 2009 x 0.1364 t/bbl (1/7.33 barrels per tonne of oil equivalent, Wikipedia Tonne of oil equivalent) = 1.66 Gt; original oil in place about 35 Gbbl and recoverable reserves are not given, so production only is a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Oil & Gas Journal, SPE: Pemex aspires for 60% oil recovery from Cantarell, https://www.ogj.com/home/article/17277366/spe-pemex-aspires-for-60-oil-recovery-from-cantarell : "originally contained about 35 billion bbl of oil in place"; "To date, Pemex has produced about 12.2 billion bbl" (7 October 2009)

entries.name: Bolivar Coastal Fields
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Lake Maracaibo east shore; ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Recoverable oil, past and future, 30 to 32 Gb; midpoint 31 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl = 4.23 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Bolivar Coastal Fields, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivar_Coastal_Fields : "ranked #5 in the world in recoverable oil, past and future at 30-32 billion barrels"

entries.name: Kirkuk (Baba Gurgur)
entries.source: Coordinate from memory (Kirkuk city is 35.47N 44.39E). Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Recoverable oil 10 Gb (infobox; the page also gives over 10 Gb proven remaining in 1998, so production is not included) x 0.1364 t/bbl = 1.36 Gt; a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Kirkuk Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirkuk_Field : "Recoverable oil 10,000 million barrels"; "over 10 billion barrels ... of proven remaining oil reserves in 1998"

entries.name: East Texas
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia: over 5.42 billion barrels produced to date; remaining reserves small.
entries.contained_basis: Produced over 5.42 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl = 0.739 Gt; remaining reserves not given, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, East Texas Oil Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Texas_Oil_Field : "Over 5.42 billion barrels ... of oil have been produced from it to-date"

entries.name: Samotlor
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: About 2.6 Gt produced and the field 80% depleted: 2.6 / 0.8 = 3.25 Gt (derived)
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Samotlor Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samotlor_Field : "about 2.6 billion tons of oil has been produced"; "The field is 80% depleted"

entries.name: Romashkino
entries.source: Coordinate from memory (Almetyevsk area, Tatarstan); ultimately recoverable order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Some 3.5 Gt of oil extracted by July 2025 as stated; remaining not given, so a lower bound (the page's statistical depletion estimate of 16.5-17.2 Gb is lower and is not used)
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Romashkino Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romashkino_Field : "some 3.5 billion tonnes of oil had been extracted by July 2025"

entries.name: Hassi Messaoud
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Renamed from hassi_messaoud_gas: it is an oil field. Ultimately recoverable, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Total proven reserves 870 Mt (6.4 Gb; the infobox calls it oil in place), undated; production not added
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Hassi Messaoud oil field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hassi_Messaoud_oil_field : "total proven reserves of the Hassi Messaoud oil field are around 6.4 billion barrels (870 million tonnes)"

entries.name: Tengiz
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia: recoverable 6-9 billion barrels. The earlier entry was in the wrong place (43.2N 69.2E, near Taraz).
entries.contained_basis: Recoverable reserves estimated 6 to 9 Gb; midpoint 7.5 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl = 1.02 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Tengiz field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tengiz_field : "recoverable reserves estimated at between six billion and nine billion barrels"

entries.name: Kashagan
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia: recoverable about 13 billion barrels. The earlier entry was 18 degrees of longitude off.
entries.contained_basis: Recoverable 13 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl = 1.77 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Kashagan Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashagan_Field : "recoverable reserves of about 13 billion barrels"

entries.name: Baku (Absheron peninsula)
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Seeps worked since antiquity; cumulative output of the Absheron fields, order of magnitude from memory. Replaces baku_oil_seeps.
entries.contained_basis: SOCAR history gives over one billion tons of Azerbaijani oil produced by 1949, when almost all output came from the Absheron peninsula (the offshore Oil Rocks field started that year); production only, a lower bound. National cumulative to 2024 is 2.22 Gt but includes Caspian offshore fields
entries.contained_source: SOCAR, Oil history of Azerbaijan, https://socar.jobs/en/page/oil-history-of-azerbaijan : "1949 ... Azerbaijan reached over one billion tons of oil production"; Trend, https://www.trend.az/business/energy/3893965.html : "Azerbaijan has produced 2.22 billion tons of oil" in the history of field development

entries.name: Hit bitumen seeps
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Seeps worked since the Bronze Age; no defensible endowment figure, omitted. hit_iraq_seeps and hit_seeps_bitumen merged here.

entries.name: Pitch Lake, Trinidad
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Order ten million tonnes of asphalt in production plus remaining, from memory; grade is kilograms of bitumen per tonne of lake asphalt. pitch_lake_bitumen merged here.
entries.contained_basis: Pitch Lake estimated to contain 10 million tons of bitumen (tons taken as metric)
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Pitch Lake, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitch_Lake : "the largest natural deposit of bitumen in the world, estimated to contain 10 million tons"

entries.name: Athabasca oil sands
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Recoverable bitumen, production plus reserves; in-place figure is about an order larger. From memory.
entries.contained_basis: Alberta estimate for Athabasca: 35 Gb surface-mineable + 98 Gb recoverable in situ = 133 Gb x 0.1364 t/bbl (crude factor; bitumen is denser so this understates) = 18.1 Gt; production not added
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Athabasca oil sands, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athabasca_oil_sands : "the Athabasca deposits alone contain 35 billion barrels of surface mineable bitumen and 98 billion barrels of bitumen recoverable by in-situ methods"

entries.name: Orinoco Belt
entries.source: Coordinate approximate (belt centre); certified reserves of order two hundred billion barrels, USGS technically recoverable estimate is larger. From memory.
entries.contained_basis: Producible reserves of the Orinoco Belt up to 235 Gb (PDVSA estimate) x 0.1364 t/bbl (crude factor; extra-heavy crude is denser so this understates tonnes) = 32.1 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Orinoco Belt, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orinoco_Belt : "the producible reserves of the Orinoco Belt are up to 235 billion barrels"

entries.name: South Pars (Iranian share of North Dome)
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Iranian share of the shared field, order of magnitude from memory; the whole field is about three times larger.
entries.contained_basis: Whole South Pars/North Dome field recoverable gas 36,000e9 m3 x 0.717 kg/m3 (Wikipedia Methane) = 25.8 Gt; the Iranian share is not given on the page, so this is the whole shared field
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, South Pars Gas Field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pars_Gas_Field : "Recoverable gas 1,260,000 x 10^9 cu ft (36,000 x 10^9 m3)"

entries.name: Urengoy
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Initial reserves of order ten trillion cubic metres, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Over 10 trillion m3 (1e13) in total deposits x 0.717 kg/m3 (methane gas at 0 C, Wikipedia Methane, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methane) = 7.17 Gt gas
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Urengoy gas field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urengoy_gas_field : "over ten trillion cubic meters (10^13 m3) in total deposits"

entries.name: Groningen
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Wikipedia: estimated 2,740 billion cubic metres recoverable.
entries.contained_basis: 2,740 billion m3 recoverable methane x 0.717 kg/m3 (Wikipedia Methane) = 1.96 Gt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Groningen gas field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groningen_gas_field : "estimated 2,740 billion cubic metres of recoverable methane"; 2,057 billion m3 extracted by 2013

entries.name: Troll
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Recoverable gas, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Troll East total recoverable reserves 1,330.7 billion Sm3 gas x 0.717 kg/m3 = 954 Mt; Troll West gas not added, so a lower bound for the field
entries.contained_source: Norwegian Petroleum Museum, The Troll area, https://www.norskolje.museum.no/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/3467_321daaaf2b0644d897762f3bb73224cc.pdf : "Troll East: Total recoverable reserves 1 330.7 bn scm gas" (remaining 995 bn scm at 31 Dec 2008)

entries.name: Lacq
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Initial reserves about a quarter of a trillion cubic metres, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Estimated gas in place 251 billion m3 x 0.717 kg/m3 (Wikipedia Methane) = 0.18 Gt; in place, not recoverable, and the gas is sour
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Lacq gas field, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacq_gas_field : "Estimated gas in place 251 x 10^9 m3"

entries.name: Bayu-Undan
entries.source: Timor Sea; coordinate and recoverable gas (about three to four trillion cubic feet) from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Gross 2P sales gas and ethane 3.8 tcf at end 2003 (before first production in 2004) x 28.317 billion m3 per tcf = 107.6 billion m3 x 0.717 kg/m3 = 77.2 Mt; the 530 million barrels of condensate and LPG are not added
entries.contained_source: Santos, Bayu-Undan Liquids (page of 6 October 2005, mirrored by La'o Hamutuk), https://www.laohamutuk.org/OilWeb/Company/Santos/SantosBU.htm : "2003 Year End Reserves (Gross 2P) ... Sales gas and ethane (TCF) 3.8"

entries.name: Powder River Basin
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus recoverable reserves, order of magnitude from memory; in-place resource is far larger.
entries.contained_basis: USGS original coal resource 1.16 trillion short tons x 0.9072 = 1,052 Gt (a resource estimate for 47 beds; recoverable coal reserve base 162 Bst = 147 Gt; reserves 25 Bst = 22.7 Gt)
entries.contained_source: USGS Professional Paper 1809, Luppens and others, 2015, https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/pp1809 : "an original coal resource of about 1.16 trillion short tons for 47 coal beds in the Powder River Basin"; "162 billion short tons of recoverable coal resources"; "25 billion short tons ... met the definition of reserves" (2015)

entries.name: Appalachian coalfields
entries.source: Production plus reserves across the region, order of magnitude from memory; coordinate approximate.
entries.contained_basis: Cumulative production 34.5 Bst (to about 2000) + 66 Bst remaining in five selected beds (Pittsburgh, Upper Freeport, Fire Clay, Pond Creek, Pocahontas No. 3) = 100.5 Bst x 0.9072 = 91.2 Gt; other beds not counted, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: USGS Fact Sheet 004-02, Coal Resources of Selected Coal Beds and Zones in the Northern and Central Appalachian Basin, https://pubs.usgs.gov/fs/fs004-02/fs004-02.html : "the cumulative production is estimated at 34.5 billion short tons"; "Of the 93 billion short tons of original coal in these units, about 66 billion short tons remain" (2002)

entries.name: Illinois Basin
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus recoverable reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: About 11 Bst produced to 2005 + almost 52 Bst potential coal reserve = 63 Bst x 0.9072 = 57.2 Gt
entries.contained_source: USGS Professional Paper 1625-F Chapter H, Milici and others, 2005, https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/1625f/downloads/ChapterH.pdf : "About 11 billion tons of coal has been produced from the Illinois Basin"; "the basin contains almost 52 billion tons of coal as a potential coal reserve" (2005)

entries.name: Kuznetsk Basin
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Resource estimate for the whole basin, 725 Gt; how much is reserve and how much past production is not stated, and it is far above the mineable fraction
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Kuznetsk Basin, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuznetsk_Basin : "Overall coal deposits are estimated at 725 billion tonnes"

entries.name: Ordos Basin
entries.source: Shaanxi-Shanxi-Inner Mongolia coal; reserves plus production, order of magnitude from memory; coordinate approximate.
entries.contained_basis: Proven coal reserves of Ordos city 210.2 Gt (2021); assumes the city's proven reserves stand for the Ordos Basin coalfield (the city covers the basin's main coal area, assumption); production not added
entries.contained_source: China Daily, Coal industry hits development milestone in Ordos, https://regional.chinadaily.com.cn/ordosen/en/2021-12/06/c_692839.htm : "The city has proven coal reserves of 210.2 billion metric tons"

entries.name: Donets Basin
entries.source: Resources plus production, order of magnitude from memory; coordinate approximate.
entries.contained_basis: Estimated reserves 60 Gt (year not stated); production since the 1800s not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Donets Basin, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donets_Basin : "with estimated reserves of 60 billion tonnes of coal"

entries.name: Bowen Basin
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Resource plus production, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Known black coal resources of the north Bowen Basin about 47 Gt (a resource, not reserves; production not added; south Bowen not included)
entries.contained_source: Geoscience Australia, North Bowen Basin region: Discovered resources data guide, https://ecat.ga.gov.au/geonetwork/srv/api/records/da865371-31dd-484a-b4db-0997060d0719 : "known black coal resources of approximately 47 billion tonnes"

entries.name: Sydney Basin
entries.source: Wikipedia gives the basin centre at 33.95S 150.76E, but the working coalfields (Newcastle, Hunter, Illawarra) lie across the whole basin; production plus resource, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Remaining black coal at end 2022 in the Sydney Basin: economic demonstrated 15,757 Mt + subeconomic demonstrated 509 Mt + inferred 10,211 Mt = 26,477 Mt; production since 1797 is not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Geoscience Australia, Australia's Energy Commodity Resources 2024, Coal, Table 4.1, https://www.ga.gov.au/aecr2024/coal : Sydney Basin row, EDR 15,757 Mt, SDR 509 Mt, Inferred 10,211 Mt (end 2022)

entries.name: Great Northern Coalfield (Newcastle, UK)
entries.source: Cumulative production, order of magnitude from memory; coordinate approximate.
entries.contained_basis: Estimated tons of coal in the Durham and Northumberland coalfield at depths down to 4,000 feet, as tabulated in a 1920s book that cites the 1925 Royal Commission on the Coal Industry; the book's unit is tons (treated as tonnes, within 2%); past production not added
entries.contained_source: The Basic Industries of Great Britain, ch. 1, https://digi.econbiz.de/viewer/fulltext/1747397008/20/ : "Durham and Northumberland . 10,780,741,987" (estimated tons)

entries.name: Ruhr coalfield
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Cumulative production, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Estimated reserves 42 Gt (BGR 2012 as cited); cumulative production since the 1800s is not on the page, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Ruhr coalfield, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruhr_coalfield : "estimated reserves of 42 billion tonnes of coal" (citing a 2012 BGR report)

entries.name: Jharia coalfield
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Resource of the order of twenty billion tonnes, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Estimated reserves 19.4 Gt coking coal (year not stated); production not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Jharia Coalfield, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jharia_Coalfield : "having estimated reserves of 19.4 billion tonnes of coking coal"

entries.name: Witbank (Mpumalanga) coalfield
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Council for Geoscience reserves for Witbank in 1982 = 12,461 Mt; 3,952 Mt was produced from 1982 to 2009 and 8,509 Mt remained in 2009; production before 1982 is not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: McGill, The Coal Value Chain (CSIR, 2015), Table 1.1, https://researchspace.csir.co.za/bitstream/handle/10204/8153/McGill_2015.pdf : Witbank, Reserves 1982 12 461.0 Mt, ROM production 1982-2009 3 951.7 Mt, remaining 2009 8 509.3 Mt

entries.name: Upper Silesian Coal Basin
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus resource, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Page says the basin 'contains about 70 billion tons' (year and ton type not stated; taken as metric); production not added
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Upper Silesian Coal Basin, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Silesian_Coal_Basin : "contains about 70 billion tons, with good extraction potential"
